summary: Plumas County, CA ground lookout south of Quincy; planned in 1907, in use by 1909 and maintained in 1911; listed as gone, with no later record found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source we read describes what remains on the mountain.

events.note: Plan for a telephone line, a summer ranger camp and a fire-season lookout station; not yet built at the time
Bulletin says the station would be maintained for the summer season; staffing is not named
Claremont and Mount Hough lookout peaks to be maintained, each with telephone connection to headquarters

evidence.supports: Claremont Mountain is in the Plumas National Forest
station on Claremont Mountain south of Quincy
evidence.quote: The fire lookout station on Claremont Mountain south of Quincy

evidence.supports: Plumas County; listed as a ground site, gone
1907 plan: telephone line next season, summer ranger camp, lookout station in fire season
evidence.quote: It is planned to run a telephone line next season to the summit of Claremont mountain, establish a summer ranger camp there, and have this a lookout station during the fire season.

evidence.supports: November 1907: branch line from Quincy in spring; lookout to be established in dry months
evidence.quote: In the spring a branch line will be built from Quincy to the summit of Claremont mountain, where a fire lookout will be established during the dry summer months.

evidence.supports: May 1909: station to be maintained through the summer season
evidence.quote: The fire lookout station on Claremont Mountain south of Quincy will be maintained for the summer season

evidence.supports: November 1909: station credited with locating fires
evidence.quote: The fire lookout station maintained on Claremont Mountain proved of such great assistance in locating fires the past summer

evidence.supports: 85 fires extinguished or helped to extinguish that season on or next to the Plumas Forest
evidence.quote: the Forest officers extinguished or helped to extinguish 85 fires on or adjacent to the Plumas Forest

evidence.supports: June 1911: Claremont and Mount Hough to be maintained
evidence.quote: The two lookout peaks--Claremont and Mount Hough--will be maintained.

evidence.supports: each station with telephone connection to headquarters
evidence.quote: Each station is equipped with telephone connection with headquarters here

sources.title: Claremont Mountain (Forest Lookouts, with transcribed Plumas newspaper items)

notes_for_editor: History is good through 1911 but comes from transcribed newspaper items; no source after 1911 was found. The FFLA list gives 'Ground Gone' with no year, so the loss date and cause are unknown. No construction record exists; 1909 'maintained' is read as staffing. Unread lead: a search snippet of an FFLA Facebook #tbt post describes a 1911 lookout point with a telephone line and a structure built later that year; the page would not load, so it is not used and it may concern Claremont or Mount Hough. Peakbagging lists 'Claremont (LO site)'. No photos found.
